subject: english-literature
title: Voices on the Page
welcome_lead: Step into the first area of exploration: how writers craft texts and how readers make meaning. Narrative voice, focalisation, and language choices shape every reading experience.
meta_desc: English Literature: Readers, Writers & Texts — narrative voice, focalisation, reader response, and stylistic devices.
final_note: You have entered the conversation between writer, text, and reader. Keep listening for the voice behind the words.

concepts.def: The persona through which a story is told; may be first person, third person limited, or omniscient.
Gerard Genette's term for the perspective through which narrative information is filtered.
Wolfgang Iser's theory that meaning emerges through the reader's active engagement with textual gaps.
The distinctive manner of expression, including diction, syntax, and rhythm.
The author's choice of words and their connotations.
The hypothetical reader that the text seems to address and shape.

walkthroughs.body_html: Ask: who speaks, and from where? A first-person narrator (I) gives intimacy but limits perspective. Third-person omniscient knows all minds; third-person limited stays close to one consciousness. Watch for shifts: a sudden change in voice often signals thematic weight.

Genette separates who speaks (voice) from who sees (focalisation). Internal focalisation filters events through one character's senses and thoughts; external focalisation reports only what is visible. Zero focalisation is the godlike, knowing-all stance.

Iser argued texts contain Leerstellen — gaps the reader fills with inference. A novel that withholds a motive invites the reader to construct one. Your essay can analyse how a passage shapes the reader's role.

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.

mcqs.q: What defines epic poetry as a genre?
options: Context is required because all texts are about history.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Epic means any poem that is very long.
Long narrative poems on heroic subjects, in elevated style, often invoking a muse, in medias res openings, and treating events of national or cosmic significance.

mcqs.q: Why does historical context matter when reading literature?
options: Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Context just means writing about what the author had for breakfast.
Context is required because all texts are about history.
Texts emerge from and respond to specific historical conditions — context illuminates references, assumptions and arguments that might otherwise be invisible.
